name: Jackson Falls Dispersed Primitive Camping Area - Shawnee National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Hidden Springs Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout general forest lands outside developed recreation areas. Campsites must be set back at least 150 feet from trails and natural water bodies.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in rich organic soil, at least 200 feet from streams and waterfall pools. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. All trash must be packed out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires allowed in existing rock fire rings. Extinguish with stream water until cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Illinois DNR / USFS fire warnings during dry autumn spells.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved gravel forest road (Glen Street Road / Jackson Falls Access)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Narrow gravel gravel road with potholes, dust, and small washboards.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible in dry weather along main gravel access road)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Sandstone bluff canyons and hardwood forest canopy restrict line of sight)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, high waterfall flow, blooming wildflowers, moderate mud on unpaved tracks.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (82-90°F), dense leaf canopy, high tick/mosquito activity.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal camping weather (60-75°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), stunning hardwood fall foliage.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 35-50°F, occasional freezes and light snow dustings.

dangers_and_hazards: High sandstone cliff drop-offs (climbing safety caution)
Venomous snakes: Copperheads active near bluffs in warm months
Ticks and chiggers in forest underbrush

common_human_made_sounds: Rock climbers calling out on Jackson Falls bluffs

common_plants_and_trees: French's Shooting Star (Dodecatheon frenchii - rare endemic in sandstone overhangs)

human_demographics_and_culture: Rock climbers (Jackson Falls is the top climbing destination in the Midwest), backpackers, digital nomads, and local nature photographers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Kaskaskia and Shawnee indigenous traditions revere the sandstone bluffs and hidden waterfall box canyons of southern Illinois as sacred medicine sites.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: High quartz sandstone acoustic resonance, soothing waterfall ions, peaceful forest sanctuary.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding path along base of 60-foot sandstone bluffs and waterfalls

public_reviews_summary: Premier free primitive camping spot for rock climbers and nature lovers in southern Illinois. Great scenery and reliable cell coverage.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Abundant deadwood.
